newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia raises '97 agricultural benchmark prices.
newsitem.headline: Croatia raises '97 agricultural benchmark prices.

text.p: Croatia's government Thursday raised the benchmark price of some agricultural goods and announced more than a million hectars of arable land would be sown in 1997, state media reported.
The government raised benchmark prices by 4.8-11.1 percent for wheat, soy, tobacco and sunflower while sugar beet was priced the same as last year, at 0.22 kuna per kilo, HINA news agency said.
The benchmark prices represent the subsidy for agriculture, as the government planned to buy surplus stocks.
The government said crops would be grown at 1.20 million hectares of arable land.
"I can say input in spring sowing nears some 1.6 billion kuna, while the expected output should be around 3.7 billion kuna," Croatian radio quoted Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic as saying.
